children: Harvey Norman's stable property portfolio helps stop Macquarie analysts turning sour on the Australian furniture and homewares retailer. The analysts tell clients in a note that the rate of decline in Harvey Norman's earnings is a concern, with consumers laboring under cost-of-living pressures. They think that the company's unusual decision to comment on earnings this early in a fiscal year is a negative signal for market expectations. However, its property portfolio accounts for about 50% of Macquarie's sum-of-the-parts valuation and they think that limits downside for the stock. Macquarie cuts its target price 4.8%, to 4.00 Australian dollars. Shares are at A$4.13 ahead of the open. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
